steps.body: A **flat** shape (triangle, square, hexagon) lies on the page — it's 2D. A **solid** shape (cube, cone, cylinder) takes up space — it's 3D. You could hold a solid shape in your hand.

options.label: 2D
options.feedback: Yes — a hexagon is flat, so it's 2D.

options.label: 3D
options.feedback: A hexagon lies flat on the page — it's 2D, not 3D.

explanationVariants: A cube takes up space, so it's 3D.
You could hold a cube — that makes it 3D, not flat.

options.label: 3D
options.feedback: Yes — a cube takes up space, so it's 3D.

options.label: 2D
options.feedback: A cube isn't flat — it takes up space, so it's 3D.

steps.body: Solids have flat faces, curved surfaces, or both. A cube is made only of flat faces. A cone has one flat face (its circle base) and one curved surface.

predict.prompt: A cube is a solid box. Before counting — how many flat faces does it have?

options.label: 4 — just the sides you can see

predict.reveal: A cube has a face on every side: top, bottom, front, back, left and right — six in all. The ones facing away still count, which is why the dashed lines matter.

widget.prompt: Touch each flat face of the cube to count it. The dashed lines show the faces round the back.
widget.successFeedback: 6 faces! A cube has six flat square faces — top, bottom, front, back, and two sides.
widget.missedFeedback: Some faces are still uncounted. The dashed lines lead to the ones at the back.
widget.doubleCountFeedback: That face is already counted. Tap it again to let it go.

steps.body: A cylinder has two flat faces (the circles at top and bottom) and one curved surface wrapping around the side.

widget.prompt: Touch each FLAT face of the cylinder. The curved part that wraps around is not flat.
widget.successFeedback: 2 flat faces — the circle on top and the circle on the bottom. The part that wraps around is curved, not flat.
widget.missedFeedback: There is one more flat face. Look at the other end.
widget.doubleCountFeedback: That face is already counted. Tap it again to let it go.

explanationVariants: A triangle is flat, so it's 2D.
You can't hold a triangle — it lies flat on the page.

options.label: 2D
options.feedback: Yes — a triangle is flat, so it's 2D.

options.label: 3D
options.feedback: A triangle lies flat on the page — it's 2D, not 3D.

explanationVariants: A cone has 1 flat face — its circle base.
Only the base is flat; the rest curves up to the point.

widget.prompt: How many flat faces does a cone have?

commonErrors.feedback: A cone only has ONE flat face — the base. The rest is curved.
The circle base of a cone IS flat. It has 1 flat face.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A cone has 1 flat face (its base).

explanationVariants: A cylinder has 1 curved surface — the side that wraps around.
The top and bottom are flat; the wrap-around side is the 1 curved surface.

widget.prompt: How many curved surfaces does a cylinder have?

commonErrors.feedback: The curved part wraps all the way around as ONE surface, not two.
The side of a cylinder curves — that's 1 curved surface.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A cylinder has 1 curved surface (the side).

hints: Think about the side that wraps around the cylinder.
It curves all the way around as one piece.

steps.body: Flat shapes are 2D; shapes that take up space are 3D, with flat faces and/or curved surfaces.
takeaways: Cubes are all flat faces; cones and cylinders mix flat and curved.
steps.teaser: next: naming more solid shapes by their faces.

concept.body: Flat shapes (triangle, hexagon) are 2D — they lie on the page. Solids (cube, cone, cylinder) are 3D — they take up space, made of flat faces and/or curved surfaces.
